deities: Kancha Kanti Devi (union of Goddesses Kali and Durga)

history.summary: Town corrected: the temple stands at Udharbond (Udarbond), about 15-17 km from Silchar on the way to the airport — not in Silchar town itself. Legend says the Kachari king established a four-armed gold image of the goddess here in 1806 after being commanded in a dream; one video source names the king as Govinda Chandra Narayan of the Kachari dynasty. The goddess Kanchakanti ('golden radiance') is worshipped as a combined form of Kali and Durga, standing on Lord Shiva. The old temple was destroyed by natural forces and the present structure was built in 1978; a Kachakanti Vidya Mandir school stands nearby. Folklore also mentions human sacrifice having once been practised here (unverified).

name: Sri Kancha Kanti Devi Temple
town_description: Udharbond (Udarbond) is a small town about 15 km northeast of Silchar in Cachar district, on the road toward Silchar (Kumbhirgram) Airport. It is best known for the Kanchakanti temple and the nearby Brajamohan Goswami Ashram.

travel.airport: Silchar Airport (Kumbhirgram, IXS), on the same road about 15-20 km away
travel.railway: Silchar Railway Station (SCL), about 15 km away
travel.road: Town on the Silchar-Udharbond airport road; reachable by taxi, auto-rickshaw, or bus from Silchar

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (cooler months); also during Durga Puja and Kali Puja
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily (travelsetu; some sources say 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM — verify locally). No entry fee; offerings and donations are customary. Photography inside the sanctum may be restricted.
